{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-me-c","lineage":{"candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-me-class-c:lineage:19","input_manifest_sha256":"5fac7e8129615ce37680a65e2f0a4899d612944bef2812c0a387de03d38fe944","source_registry_sha256":"c2e42c38f9f4644827a2fdadadd6340aab123a85c208ecc4839848339c6c9a98","source_liveness_sha256":"e742bf2373c9a6bebd7774b2b45ae2a58ba395947586ea942f331e99a0744f40"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Your Driver’s License","heading":"C — Your Driver’s License","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Your Driver’s License

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A06
Keep your attention on driving and remain ready to stop, swerve or change speed to prevent a collision. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A07
A Maine resident needs a Maine license to drive in the state, subject to the listed permit and other exemptions. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A07
A new resident with a valid license from another state must surrender it and seek a Maine license within 30 days after establishing residency. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A07
A resident with a valid learner permit may drive with a licensed supervisor aged at least 20 who has held a valid license for at least 2 years. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A07
The licensed supervisor accompanying a resident permit holder must sit next to the learner. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A07
A nonresident aged at least 16 may drive in Maine with a valid operator license or learner permit issued by the home state. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A07
Military personnel driving a military vehicle may rely on a valid military license. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A07
A Maine learner-permit applicant must be at least 15 years old. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A07
A permit applicant younger than 18 must finish an approved driver-education course. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A07
Obtaining a learner permit requires passing the driver-knowledge written examination. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A07
A learner permit generally lasts 2 years. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A07
The person supervising a permit holder must hold a license covering the vehicle class being driven. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A07
The manual’s learner-permit guidance prohibits driving while using a mobile phone or a handheld electronic device. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A07
Written examinations and vision screenings at motor-vehicle branches are scheduled. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A07
The permit application guidance calls for 2 identification documents. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A07
Applicants must provide a Social Security number when applying for or renewing a license, although it is absent from the license display. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A07
Applicants aged 22 or younger need a birth certificate or passport to establish their date of birth. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A07
A birth-certificate photocopy needs the issuing agency’s embossed seal or stamp; a notarized copy is unacceptable. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A08
Class C is the standard Maine license category issued to most drivers. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A08
A driver may qualify for a license at age 16 after completing approved driver education. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A08
Without approved driver education, the minimum age for obtaining a license is 18. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A08
Before requesting a road test, an applicant younger than 21 must have held the learner permit for 6 months from its issue date. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A08
Before applying for a road test, a person younger than 21 must complete at least 70 hours of driving after the learner permit is issued, including 10 at night, while accompanied by a licensed driver aged at least 20 who has held a valid license for 2 years. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A09
A road-test applicant must successfully complete the road test to obtain the license. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A09
To request a road test, mail the issued request form or driving log to the main Motor Vehicles office in Augusta. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A09
Bring the learner permit and appointment notice to the scheduled road test. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A09
A road-test applicant supplies a registered, inspected vehicle and brings its registration. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A09
A road-test applicant must arrive with a licensed operator carrying a valid driver license. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A09
When snow or ice affects a scheduled road-test day, the applicant may choose rescheduling without a fee. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A09
A newly licensed driver younger than 18 may not use a mobile phone or handheld electronic device while driving. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A09
A newly licensed driver younger than 18 may not drive from 12 a.m. through 5 a.m. during the initial restriction period. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A09
During the initial restriction period, a driver younger than 18 may carry nonfamily passengers only with an adjacent supervisor aged at least 20 who has held a valid license for 2 years and is licensed for that vehicle class. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A09
The initial restrictions for newly licensed drivers younger than 18 last 270 days after passing the road test. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A09
Violating an initial underage-license restriction brings a suspension and a further 270 restriction days that can extend past the eighteenth birthday. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A09
A first license is provisional for 2 years when issued before age 21, and for 1 year when issued at age 21 or older. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A09
A moving-violation conviction for conduct while driving on a provisional license causes a 30-day suspension. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A09
The written test covers traffic law, regulations, driving skills, vehicle handling and highway-sign understanding, with particular attention to Maine’s drinking-and-driving laws. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A09
The vision screening checks visual sharpness and side vision while looking ahead. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A10
The road-test examiner evaluates vehicle control and responses to traffic, pedestrians, signs, signals and road conditions. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A10
A road test follows successful completion of all the other tests. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A10
An initial-license applicant must take every required examination. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F42 | anchor: A10
A valid out-of-state license may allow the written and road tests to be waived. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F43 | anchor: A10
A driver transferring a license must be at least 16 to apply for a Maine license. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F44 | anchor: A10
A transferring driver aged 16 or 17 may have to show completion of approved driver education. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F45 | anchor: A10
An out-of-state license must be surrendered when Maine issues the replacement license. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F46 | anchor: A10
A false statement on a license application causes immediate revocation of the license and Maine driving privilege, and may lead to court action. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F47 | anchor: A11
After passing the required tests, a driver younger than 65 may buy a photo license valid until the sixth birthday following issuance. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F48 | anchor: A11
For an applicant aged 65 or older, a photo license lasts until the fourth birthday after issuance. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F49 | anchor: A11
Photo-license processing requires evidence of lawful presence and legal residency. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F50 | anchor: A11
An applicant younger than 18 must bring a parent or legal guardian to sign for photo-license issuance. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F51 | anchor: A11
Carry the driver license while driving and show it when a police officer requests it. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F52 | anchor: A11
Lending your driver license to another person is illegal. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

Glossary: the terms in the fact statements keep their handbook meanings.
Dynamic facts: officeholders, contact details and current administrative levels are excluded from stable learner facts and held in the accuracy notes.
